Attachment-7: Initial Engineering Design and Cost Estimate 2 DE-FE0031937 / 0009 1.0 Background Dastur International Inc. has designed and engineered an amine solvent-based pre-combustion carbon capture system solution that maximizes the decarbonization of available BF gas by capturing up to 2.8 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) of carbon dioxide (CO ) emissions from blast furnaces (BFs) at Cleveland- 2 Cliffs’ 5-million tonnes/year steel production plant in Burns Harbor, Indiana. The project aims to design and integrate a BF gas flow distribution system, an innovative BF gas conditioning process CO , which can be 2 captured using a single train, resulting in reduced size and capital cost of the captured island, and improved overall economics on a $/t CO captured basis. 2 The available BF gas is tapped from the BF header and undergoes a compositional shift by passing it through a series of Water Gas Shift (WGS) Reactors, which converts ~80% of the carbon monoxide (CO) in the BF gas to CO . The increase in CO content (22% in BF gas vs. 32% after the WGS unit) in the shifted gas enables 2 2 the capture of up to 85% of CO e with 95% carbon capture efficiency in the available BF gas, with benefits 2 of lower capture island footprint, single train, lower CAPEX and easier fit within the space-constrained Burns Harbor plant. The post-capture H -rich fuel gas is sent to the existing powerhouse to produce captive power 2 for in-plant use; the use of the H -rich fuel gas instead of the BF gas (present scenario) in the powerhouse 2 does not require any modification to the existing burners, thus minimizing disruptions to existing operations.
